findings.source_passage: She dragged me to my butt-mark in the dirt and arranged us so we faced each other.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'butt-mark in the dirt' detail is a comic, voice-defining beat that grounds the scene in Miriam's wry self-deprecation; its absence flattens the exchange into generic action.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'butt-mark in the dirt' staging line to preserve the comic register before Heather's theory.

findings.source_passage: I was up to bartering my soul for a reprieve from the wind whipping through my hair when we reached the castle.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after 'Like any unprofessional rider I clung tightly to his neck and prayed.'
findings.why_it_matters: This comic hyperbole ('bartering my soul') is Miriam's most voice-defining line in the flight sequence and establishes her ironic register under duress; its removal leaves only bare travel fact.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'bartering my soul' line and the 'eternity for my heart' coda—they are the only voice material in the flight passage.

findings.source_passage: I wondered how many doors were shut to this priestly fellow.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'He led me through the maze of corridors'
findings.why_it_matters: This aside is a characteristic narratorial digression—dry humor amid crisis—that establishes the narrator's refusal to surrender irony even in a desperate scene; erasing it flattens voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the 'I wondered how many doors were shut to this priestly fellow' interjection after the guards bow and open the door.

findings.source_passage: Like any unprofessional rider I clung tightly to his neck and prayed.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after Apuleius sweeps Miriam into his arms
findings.why_it_matters: A small but characteristically self-mocking line that marks Miriam's voice; its loss is minor but consistent with a pattern of comic-aside erasure in this draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore this line when describing the airborne departure.

findings.source_passage: She grinned. 'I'll always be there to give you the good news, now get going.'
findings.source_locator: farewell exchange between Miriam and Heather, after 'Thanks. That really helps.'
findings.why_it_matters: Heather's parting quip is a small character-voice beat that closes the human-world segment on a note of warmth and comedy; the draft cuts it, ending the farewell abruptly.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Heather's 'I'll always be there to give you the good news' line before Miriam leaps.

summary: Three medium-severity voice-flattening losses—the 'butt-mark in the dirt' staging beat, the 'bartering my soul' flight hyperbole, and the 'I wondered how many doors' priestly aside—collectively erase the chapter's comic-ironic register and trigger regeneration.
